newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico opposition sees gains in lower house - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico opposition sees gains in lower house - paper.

text.p: The conservative National Action Party (PAN) could win a majority in Mexico's lower house of Congress and the race for governor in three states up for grabs this year, a local newspaper quoted a leading PAN member and state governor as saying on Thursday.

Vicente Fox, governor of the state of Guanajuato, said his party could win a majority in the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house of Congress, from the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which has held the presidency and dominated Congress since 1929.

Fox also predicted the PAN could take governors' palaces in the northern industrial state of Nuevo Leon, the central state of San Luis Potosi and Pacific coast state Colima, the newspaper El Norte said.

Nonetheless, Fox admitted the PAN was losing ground in its campaign to win the first ever election for Mayor of Mexico City on July 6, because its candidate, Carlos Castillo Peraza was to be excluded from a television debate between two other leading candidates, he said.
"But that will not stop the PAN's overall advance being very solid," Fox was quoted as saying.

Mexicans will go to the polls on July 6 to replace the entire lower house of Congress and one-quarter of the Senate, and to choose the mayor of Mexico City and governors for Colima and San Luis Potosi. Elections for the governor of Nuevo Leon will be held on August 17.
